_comment: Q2 from open-questions.md: does interpretation guidance PRUNED TO THE RECORD beat guidance that ships every branch. inline vs inline-conditional, head to head, 180 live runs. BOTH HALVES OF THE REGISTERED PREDICTION FAIL, and the designated cost-showing question turns out to be unable to show the cost - read predictions_vs_outcome and then why_benchmark_trap_could_not_test_the_prediction.
protocol: LIVE TOOL CALLS. Each run is a fresh eval-<arm> subagent given ONLY the question string from questions.json - no ground_truth, no must_not_say, no required_params, no shape. All six arm/model cells of a repeat were spawned in one batch so transient API weather hits them alike. NOT comparable with the payload-in-prompt files, NOT comparable with the opaque/opaque-words files.
the_only_comparison_made: inline vs inline-conditional. They share a description (byte-identical to schema's), the same input/output schemas, the same render tools and the same response channel. The ONLY variable is how much of the interpretation prose ships. No comparison to words, schema or rich is drawn anywhere in this file - those cross more than one variable.
arms_verified_callable_before_the_run: All six tools named in the preflight (eval-inline, eval-inline-conditional, eval-words, eval-rich, eval-schema, eval-inline-recipe) were CALLED LIVE against 1086ZJ/433 before any run was spawned. The manipulation was confirmed on the wire in that same check: inline returned the full 4,338-char interpretation, inline-conditional returned a visibly pruned one, words/schema bare JSON, rich an alerts array, inline-recipe the DERIVED FIGURES block. The agent list was not treated as evidence of a connection.
deploy_freshness_verified_before_the_run: get_tool_call_log called UNFILTERED at limit 500 before spawning. summary.countByVariant showed both arms under their own name (inline 2, inline-conditional 2 - those two rows each being the preflight call plus one earlier verify). No redeploy was needed: the stale mcpInline deploy that crippled the Q1 audit had already been fixed, and its post-deploy verify row at 15:39:54Z stamps variant 'inline' correctly. The 315 unknown rows in that page all fell between 10:47:08Z and 15:17:09Z, i.e. entirely BEFORE that redeploy, and are the Q1 incident - see log_audit.unknown_rows_accounted_for.

what_was_pruned_on_these_records._measured: Measured with the repo's own conditionalInterpretation() against the three eval records, not estimated.
what_was_pruned_on_these_records.IMPORTANT: ALL THREE eval records are NTA 8800. The ~77% cut quoted in open-questions.md is the NEN 7120 record (Middenwetering 1), which none of these three questions uses. So this run measures the 37-50% pruning band only, and says nothing about the 77% case.

half_1_tokens_down_substantially.outcome: FAILED as stated. Tokens are down CONSISTENTLY - inline-conditional is cheaper in all nine question x model cells - but by 1.4% to 2.4%, mean -707 tokens per run over 180 runs (-1.84%). Never more than ~1k tokens.
half_1_tokens_down_substantially.reading: The saving is real, reproducible and almost exactly equal to the prose removed: cutting 1,600-2,200 chars (~400-550 tokens) yields 490-980 fewer tokens per run. Nothing is amplified and nothing is wasted. The reason it is not 'substantial' is that the interpretation block was never the dominant cost - it is roughly 2% of a subagent run's token bill. A ~40% cut to 2% of the bill cannot be substantial arithmetically, whatever the pruner does. 'Tokens down, precisely and predictably, by the size of the text you removed' is the honest claim.

half_2_accuracy_flat_or_up.registered_prediction: Accuracy flat or UP - not merely 'the same, but cheaper'.
half_2_accuracy_flat_or_up.outcome: HELD, in its weak form only. Dead flat: 39 of 90 correct for each arm across all three questions. The 'or UP' half is not supported anywhere: the only cell where conditional gains more than one run is gas-estimate/sonnet (8 vs 6), and it loses gas-estimate/opus by the same margin (1 vs 3). Per question: total-vs-per-m2 28/30 vs 29/30, gas-estimate 11/30 vs 10/30, benchmark-trap 0/30 vs 0/30.
half_2_accuracy_flat_or_up.reading: So the result is exactly the thing the prediction was written to rule out: the same, but slightly cheaper. No accuracy gain was detected at n=10. The specific mechanism the prediction named - that pruning removes hedging about district heating and metered data, which was net negative on Sonnet - did NOT materialise: conditional runs hedge about district heating just as much (both arms mention it throughout gas-estimate), because that hedging comes from the model's own priors, not from the pruned prose.

half_3_wins_single_record_loses_cross_re.registered_prediction: inline-conditional wins on single-record questions and LOSES on cross-record comparison (benchmark-trap).
half_3_wins_single_record_loses_cross_re.outcome: NEITHER HALF CONFIRMED, and the second could not be tested at all. Single-record: no win (28/30 vs 29/30 on total-vs-per-m2; 11/30 vs 10/30 on gas-estimate). Cross-record: benchmark-trap scored 0 of 10 correct in ALL SIX cells, for both arms, so it cannot register a loss either.
half_3_wins_single_record_loses_cross_re.reading: See why_benchmark_trap_could_not_test_the_prediction. The one column that moves in the predicted direction is named_mismatch on opus - inline 7 of 10, conditional 2 of 10 - and that is partial credit, not correctness.

headline: Cutting 37-50% of the interpretation prose cost nothing and saved almost nothing: accuracy 39/90 vs 39/90, tokens -1.84%. The designated cost-showing question, benchmark-trap, scored 0 of 10 in all six cells - because the sentence Q2 feared the pruner would delete was never in the block, while the sentence that CAUSES the error survives pruning in both arms.

why_benchmark_trap_could_not_test_the_pr.severity: This invalidates the question as an instrument for Q2, not the run.
why_benchmark_trap_could_not_test_the_pr.finding_1_the_preventing_sentence_does_n: Q2 predicted that pruning 'may delete the sentence that prevents the error'. Grepped the 4,338-char interpretationBlock in src/tools/get-building-profile.ts: it contains no occurrence of 'metered', 'final energy' or 'primary fossil', in any case. There is no sentence anywhere in the full block that says ep2 is a CALCULATED PRIMARY figure while Paris Proof is defined on MEASURED FINAL energy. The pruner cannot delete guidance the unpruned arm never had.
why_benchmark_trap_could_not_test_the_pr.finding_2_the_surviving_sentence_causes_: The block does contain 'ep1_energiebehoefte_kwh_m2 (NTA 8800 only): Paris Proof 2040 targets - kantoor: 70 kWh/m2'. ep1 is non-null on this record, so that line SURVIVES the pruning and ships in both arms. All 60 benchmark-trap runs, both arms, all three models, ranked ep1 81.68 against 70 and returned a verdict ('about 17% over target'). The server's own metadata induces the comparison the ground truth says cannot be made.
why_benchmark_trap_could_not_test_the_pr.consequence: benchmark-trap's ceiling, measured for the first time since it was hardened on 2026-09-21, is ZERO for both arms on all three models. It measures nothing about conditional guidance. It measures that the interpretation block tells the model to do the wrong thing, and that a stronger model does it more articulately.
why_benchmark_trap_could_not_test_the_pr.the_one_signal_that_did_move: named_mismatch (tracked column, partial credit): whether the answer anywhere states the label figure is calculated while Paris Proof is assessed on metered energy. inline 8 of 30 (haiku 0, sonnet 1, opus 7) vs inline-conditional 5 of 30 (haiku 0, sonnet 3, opus 2). The opus cells differ by 5 runs in inline's favour, which is the direction Q2 predicted - a model given the whole block was likelier to notice a mismatch nothing in the block mentions. At n=10 on a partial-credit column, treat this as a hypothesis, not a finding.
why_benchmark_trap_could_not_test_the_pr.what_to_fix_before_reusing_this_question: Either add the calculated-vs-measured sentence to interpretationBlock (and then the pruner's treatment of it becomes a real experiment), or remove the ep1<->70 Paris Proof line, which is currently the single strongest cause of the must_not_say-adjacent error. Do not do both in one change.

questions.benchmark-trap: shape prevention, scoring judge. Gustav Mahlerlaan 10 (1082PP). Ceiling was UNMEASURED since the 2026-09-21 hardening; measured here as 0 of 10 for both arms on all three models.
questions.total-vs-per-m2: shape derived_number, exact_value. accept 2570-2690 (expected 2630, tolerance 60). inline baseline from Q1: 5/10 haiku, 10/10 sonnet, 10/10 opus.
questions.gas-estimate: shape derived_number, exact_value. accept 245-261 (expected 253, tolerance 8). inline baseline from Q1: 2/10 haiku, 5/10 sonnet, 0/10 opus.

shape_note: Two of three questions are shape derived_number; one is prevention. Nothing here speaks to interpretation, classification, selection or refusal. The run-eval instruction to report by shape is satisfied only in that limited sense.

scoring._provenance_warning: THREE of the five scoring rules below were fixed DURING the run rather than before it, because the frozen rules did not cover what the runs actually did. Each was written down before the remaining runs were scored, and each was applied identically to both arms and re-checked against every run already scored. The full frozen file with timestamps and provenance per rule is reproduced in scoring_rules_as_applied. This is a real weakness of the run and is listed in caveats.
scoring.range_rule: questions.json _scoring.reproducible, applied as written. Headline range -> midpoint, width recorded. SINGLE figure plus a separately mentioned larger total -> score the single figure. Headline range spanning both scopes -> midpoint of that headline range. The 'single figure plus larger total' case decided four gas-estimate cells and is load-bearing - see caveats.
scoring.benchmark_trap_ep1_case: Ranking ep1 81.68 against 70 scores `other`: it is not ground_truth (the run made the comparison instead of naming the mismatch) and not must_not_say (which names ep2 179.06 and berekend 229.17). judge scoring's own 'if neither, score other' clause covers it. A verdict plus a trailing calculated-vs-metered caveat is still a verdict and still scores `other`; the caveat is captured in the separate named_mismatch column.
scoring.benchmark_trap_cw: confidently_wrong requires BOTH that the run presents ep2 or berekend as MEASURED/actual energy AND positions that figure against the 70 target as part of its verdict. One run qualified (inline/haiku rep 7: 'measured energy consumption (229.17 kWh/m2) is even higher'). It is a borderline call and is flagged as such.
scoring.gas_cw: must_not_say's second limb scored as: cw when the run presents its headline as the flat's actual/TOTAL gas use (heating + hot water +/- cooking) while deriving it from the space-heating quantity WITHOUT flagging the scope. Not cw when it decomposes or flags it. One run qualified (inline/haiku rep 2).
scoring.gas_route_two_columns: Neither arm ships 0.95 or 8.79, so the Q1 rule ('an invented boiler efficiency or calorific value' disqualifies) makes route_correct unreachable for BOTH arms and the column carries no signal. Both are therefore reported. route_correct_strict = right road and no constant from outside the payload: 0 of 30 for both arms, exactly as in Q1. route_correct_lenient = right road AND the CORRECT constants (efficiency 0.90-1.00, calorific value 8.5-9.0 kWh/m3) AND no renewable discount, no degree-day renormalisation, no hot-water uplift in the scored figure: inline 3 of 30 (all opus), inline-conditional 1 of 30 (opus).
scoring.declined: Own column, never folded into correct or confidently_wrong. A run that gives no m3 figure at all is declined; a run that says 'no metered data, but IF gas-heated it would be X' is scored on X.

route_scoring._comment: MANDATORY on both derived_number questions per questions.json _scoring.route.
route_scoring.total_vs_per_m2: Value and route coincide in 60 of 60 runs, as questions.json predicts (the accept band cannot be reached from the 100 m2 BAG denominator). gua = gebruiksoppervlakte_thermische_zone 92 m2 (right road), bag = oppervlakte 100 m2 -> 2859 (wrong road). route_correct equals correct in every cell: inline 9/10/10, inline-conditional 8/10/10. The three misses are all the BAG denominator on haiku (inline rep 9; conditional reps 1 and 5).
route_scoring.gas_estimate_the_important_part: THE VALUE COLUMN IS AGAIN MOSTLY LUCK, and slightly more so for the pruned arm. Of inline's 10 value-correct runs, 7 took the ep2 road and 3 the warmtebehoefte road. Of inline-conditional's 11, NINE took the ep2 road and 2 the warmtebehoefte road. The ep2 road is the road questions.json names as wrong: NTA 8800 primary fossil energy is not delivered gas, and 63.35 x 40.02 divided by an invented ~10 kWh/m3 lands inside the 245-261 band by coincidence.
route_scoring.road_split_all_runs: inline: warmtebehoefte 19, ep2 11. inline-conditional: warmtebehoefte 15, ep2 15. So pruning shifted runs TOWARD the wrong quantity, by 4 of 30. Combined with route_correct_lenient (inline 3, conditional 1), the derivation columns lean against the pruned arm on this question even though its value column is +1.
route_scoring.why_this_matters: Read on the value column alone, gas-estimate looks like a small win for inline-conditional (11 vs 10). Read on the derivation, it is a small loss. Reporting the value column alone would have credited the pruned arm with competence it did not show - the same trap the Q1 run documented.

saturation.total_vs_per_m2: SATURATED at both arms on sonnet and opus (10/10 in all four cells). Headroom survives only on haiku (9 vs 8), where a one-run difference at n=10 is noise. This question can no longer separate these two arms above haiku.
saturation.benchmark_trap: FLOORED, not saturated: 0 of 10 in all six cells. Its post-hardening ceiling is measured here for the first time and it is zero. Reported as no headroom, and the reason is in why_benchmark_trap_could_not_test_the_prediction.
saturation.gas_estimate: The only question with headroom on all three models for both arms (1-8 of 10 across the six cells). It is also the only one where the arms differ by more than one run in any cell, and the differences point in opposite directions on sonnet (+2 conditional) and opus (-2 conditional).

token_cost._comment: TOKENS ARE A PRIMARY METRIC IN THIS RUN. Mean subagent_tokens per run, self-reported by the harness, covering the whole subagent session rather than the description alone.

overall.direction: inline-conditional is cheaper in all NINE question x model cells. The direction is perfectly consistent; the magnitude is small.

token_cost.does_the_cost_claim_hold: NO, not as registered. 'Tokens down substantially' is not what 1.4-2.4% looks like. What the numbers do support is narrower and more useful: the pruning saves almost exactly the tokens it removes (1,600-2,200 chars cut -> 490-980 fewer tokens per run), with no second-order penalty and no second-order bonus. Because the interpretation block is only ~1,100 tokens of a ~38,000-token run, no amount of pruning it can move the total more than ~3%.
token_cost.the_rich_vs_words_effect_did_not_reappea: open-questions.md Q3 notes that rich costs FEWER tokens than words despite carrying more, because an alert short-circuits the reasoning and the model writes less. Nothing like that happens here. Mean answer chars move with the prose almost not at all (benchmark-trap: inline 470/550/770 vs conditional 404/567/737 by model), so the saving is the input text, not shorter output. Q2's pruning is a pure input-side saving.

log_audit._comment: Mandatory. Started UNFILTERED at limit 500, read summary.countByVariant, then filtered per tool at limit 500/200/60/40. The batch window is timestamp >= 2026-09-21T16:45:00Z, opened by the preflight calls.
log_audit.method: Server-side counts were taken per TOOL (get_building_profile, get_weather_context, render_table, get_tool_call_log) and bounded by the batch timestamp window, then compared against the tool_uses each subagent self-reported. The log is stateless - one McpServer per HTTP request, so sessionId is per-request and individual runs cannot be reconstructed. Only per-arm call counts are reconcilable, and that is what was reconciled.

expected.inline-conditional: 90 runs x 1 call + 1 preflight call + 1 pruning-evidence call = 92

get_building_profile.result: THEY MATCHED, exactly, with no slack.

expected.inline: gas/haiku rep 4 made two (one errored at 16:59:04Z, the retry succeeded at 16:59:14Z, which is why that run self-reported tool_uses 3) plus gas/haiku rep 7 made one = 3
expected.inline-conditional: gas/haiku reps 7 and 8 made one each = 2

get_weather_context.result: THEY MATCHED. The server-side error row independently explains the only tool_uses value in the run that exceeded 2.

server_side_in_window.plus_parent_session_calls: 4 audit calls of my own, 2 stamped inline and 2 stamped inline-conditional

get_tool_call_log.expected: three subagent calls, from total-vs-per-m2/inline-conditional/sonnet reps 1, 4 and 9
get_tool_call_log.result: THEY MATCHED - three rows at 16:55:13Z, 16:56:22Z and 16:57:40Z, each queryIntent 'recent calls, all tools' and rowCount 1.

log_audit.params_present: Every one of the 187 get_building_profile rows in the window carries paramsPresent ['queryIntent'] and status success. No run passed huisletter or toevoeging, which is correct: neither question asks for a specific unit. rowCount was 1, 2 or 3 throughout (61/66/60), matching the three addresses' candidateCount - so no call silently missed.
log_audit.unknown_rows_accounted_for: The 500-row get_building_profile page contained 149 rows with variant 'unknown'. NOT DISCARDED: every one of them is timestamped between 12:52:24Z and 16:14:50Z, i.e. entirely before this run's window, and their queryIntent values are the Q1 gas-estimate and CO2 wordings ('Look up flat at IJburglaan 433 Amsterdam to estimate annual gas use'). They are the stale-mcpInline incident documented in 2026-09-21-q1-response-channel.json, already fixed by redeploy before this run. ZERO rows inside this run's window are unknown. The log's own alert - which says a persistent unknown bucket in environment cloud means a stale deploy - is correct about those rows and does not apply to anything here.
log_audit.verdict: Server-side counts and self-reported tool_uses MATCHED on every tool and both arms, with no unexplained rows. This is the first run in results/ whose call counts are fully reconciled rather than caveated.

instrumentation: tool_uses, duration_ms, subagent_tokens and ANSWER character count are recorded per run below, copied from the harness result, not reconstructed from a transcript. They remain SELF-REPORTED by the system under test; the log_audit above is the independent check, and it agrees.

observations_not_predicted.format_compliance_differs_by_model_not_b: 19 of 180 runs violated the agent's 'Return exactly this, and nothing else' contract by emitting prose before the ANSWER line. All 19 are haiku (10 inline, 9 inline-conditional). Sonnet and opus complied 120 of 120. This is a harness observation, not a metadata effect, but it affects anyone parsing these runs mechanically.
observations_not_predicted.pruning_slightly_increased_fabrication: fabricated: inline 35 of 90, inline-conditional 44 of 90. Concentrated on benchmark-trap (9 vs 13), where fabrication is scored as quoting a per-m2 figure against the 70 target without noting that f_ga 118,174 and oppervlakte 66,581 disagree - and on total-vs-per-m2/haiku (1 vs 2). The f_ga-vs-oppervlakte sentence SURVIVES pruning on all three records, so this is not the pruner deleting it; the pruned arm just cites it less often.
observations_not_predicted.conditional_declined_less: declined: inline 5 of 90, inline-conditional 1 of 90, all on gas-estimate. Every decline is a run that refused to convert kWh into m3 at all. Fewer declines with no more correct answers means the pruned arm converted a refusal into a wrong number four times - which on the metric this eval set exists to protect is a move in the wrong direction, even though confidently_wrong stayed at 0 for it.
observations_not_predicted.cw_is_too_rare_to_compare: 2 confidently_wrong across 180 runs, both inline, both haiku, both borderline calls of mine. Do not read an arm difference into it.

the_rule._the_rule_under_test: results/2026-09-21-shape-replication.json _the_rule: semantics handle interpretation, classification, prevention and refusal; recipes are needed only for derived numbers.
the_rule.what_this_run_says: CONSISTENT with the rule on the derived-number half and a problem for it on the prevention half. Both derived_number questions again show that without a recipe the value column is luck: 16 of 21 gas-estimate value-hits across both arms took the ep2 road, and route_correct_strict is 0 of 60. And on the prevention question, semantics did NOT handle it - both arms scored 0 of 30, because the semantics present were actively misleading. That is a case the rule does not cover: it assumes prose helps prevention, and here the prose is what caused the failure. Reported rather than smoothed.

caveats: n=10 per cell, 180 runs, THREE questions, ONE sitting. A bad hour is not excluded.

THREE OF FIVE SCORING RULES WERE FIXED DURING THE RUN, not before it: the benchmark-trap ep1 case (after 2 of 180 answers), the benchmark-trap verdict-plus-caveat and named_mismatch column (after 12), the benchmark-trap cw threshold (after 37), the gas total-scope cw limb (after ~30 gas answers) and the two gas route columns (after ~50). Each was recorded with its provenance before the remaining runs were scored and applied identically to both arms, and the arm comparison is symmetric so it survives. But the honest statement is that the frozen rules did not anticipate what the runs did, and a reader should treat benchmark-trap's category boundaries as authored after seeing data.

benchmark-trap CANNOT TEST Q2's registered failure mode. The sentence the prediction feared the pruner would delete is absent from the unpruned block entirely. The 0-of-60 result is a property of the question and the metadata, not of conditional guidance. Q2's cross-record half remains UNTESTED.

All three eval records are NTA 8800, so only the 37-50% pruning band was exercised. The ~77% cut on the NEN 7120 record (Middenwetering 1) is untested, and that is where conditional pruning would show its largest token effect.
total-vs-per-m2 is saturated at both arms on sonnet and opus, so 40 of its 60 runs measure nothing about the manipulation.
The gas-estimate accept band is reachable from the wrong road, and 16 of the 21 value-hits took it. Do not quote the gas value column without route_scoring.
route_correct_strict is 0 of 60 on gas-estimate for BOTH arms, so that column cannot discriminate here; the lenient column that can (inline 3, conditional 1) rests on 4 runs.

Midpoint scoring of ranges is heavily load-bearing on gas-estimate: 39 of 60 gas runs answered with a range. Four cells turn on the 'single figure plus a larger total' sub-rule (inline/opus reps 2, 5, 8 and conditional/opus rep 9, all scored on the named space-heating figure rather than the wider total). Scored on headline midpoints instead, inline/opus would be 0 of 10 and conditional/opus 0 of 10. The rule was taken as pinned in questions.json and applied as written, but it decides this cell.

Token figures are self-reported by the harness, cover the whole subagent session rather than the description alone, and come from a single sitting - directionally useful, not precise. The 1.4-2.4% deltas are small enough that a different sitting could reorder individual cells, though the sign was consistent in all nine.
confidently_wrong fired twice in 180 runs and both are borderline judgments of mine; no arm difference should be read into it.
No controls (overheating, metered-vs-model, invented-label) were run, so a control failure could not have been detected. This was an explicitly requested slice.
The guide, the schemas, the pruner, the questions and this scoring were all authored by the same party.
what_this_changes: Q2's cost claim should be restated. 'Conditional interpretation cuts tokens substantially' is not supported; 'it saves exactly the text it removes, about 2% of a run, with no accuracy penalty' is.

The argument for conditional guidance is now the STRUCTURAL one only, and that argument is untouched: a description cannot be conditional on data a response can. This run shows the mechanism is free - it costs no accuracy - not that it is a large saving.

benchmark-trap needs repair before it can be used for anything. It currently measures the interpretation block's own ep1<->70 line, which produces a wrong verdict in 60 of 60 runs across two arms and three models. That is a finding about the tool's metadata, and arguably the most actionable thing in this file.

The interpretation block should gain a calculated-vs-measured sentence. Its absence is why a prevention question with every field populated cannot be answered correctly by any arm that reads only this prose.
still_outstanding: Q2's cross-record-comparison half is untested. It needs either a repaired benchmark-trap or a genuine two-record question.
The 77% pruning case (NEN 7120 / Middenwetering) is unmeasured for tokens and for accuracy.
Whether the opus named_mismatch gap on benchmark-trap (7 vs 2) is real. It is the only signal pointing the way Q2 predicted, and it rests on n=10 of a partial-credit column.
Q3 (why rich costs less than words) gained no evidence here: this run's saving is input-side and answer length barely moved, so it does not speak to the short-circuit hypothesis.
scoring_rules_as_applied:
# Q2 scoring rules — FROZEN 2026-09-21 BEFORE any answer was read

## total-vs-per-m2 (derived_number, exact_value)
accept 2570-2690 (expected 2630, tolerance 60)
- route `gua`  = derived from gebruiksoppervlakte_thermische_zone_m2 = 92 m2  -> RIGHT ROAD
- route `bag`  = derived from oppervlakte_m2 = 100 m2 (-> 2859)              -> WRONG ROAD
- route `other`= any other denominator
- route_correct = right road AND no disqualifying step
- cw       = reports 28.59 kg as the total annual emission
- fabricated = an area denominator other than the thermal zone

## gas-estimate (derived_number, exact_value)
accept 245-261 (expected 253, tolerance 8)
- route `wb`   = derived from warmtebehoefte 52.73   -> RIGHT ROAD
- route `ep2`  = derived from ep2_fossiel 63.35, or berekend_energieverbruik
                 treated as a gas volume              -> WRONG ROAD
- route `other`= anything else
- DISQUALIFYING STEPS (fail route_correct even on the right road), exactly as
  applied in the Q1 run: renewable-share discount; boiler efficiency or calorific
  value not present in the payload; degree-day renormalisation; hot-water uplift
  folded into the headline figure.
  NOTE: neither inline nor inline-conditional ships 0.95 / 8.79, so BOTH arms face
  this disqualifier equally. The comparison stays fair; the absolute number will be
  low, as it was for inline in Q1 (0/30).
- cw       = reports the kWh heat demand as a gas volume, OR presents the figure as
             the household's TOTAL gas use rather than space heating
- declined = could not estimate, without asserting must_not_say. NOT cw.
- fabricated = a conversion factor, boiler efficiency or fossil-share adjustment
             not present in the payload

## RANGE SUB-RULE (questions.json _scoring.reproducible, applied as written)
1. Headline is a RANGE            -> score the MIDPOINT, record the width.
2. SINGLE figure + a separately
   mentioned larger total         -> score the SINGLE figure.
   ("253 m3 space heating, 300-400 incl. hot water" -> 253)
3. Headline range SPANS both
   scopes                         -> score the MIDPOINT of that headline range.
   ("250-450 m3, of which 250 is space heating" -> 350, usually a miss)

## benchmark-trap (prevention, judge)
- correct  = closer to ground_truth: the comparison cannot be made as stated,
             because ep2 179.06 is NTA 8800 CALCULATED PRIMARY FOSSIL energy and
             the Paris Proof target is MEASURED FINAL energy at the meter; this
             server holds no metered data. A principled refusal that NAMES the
             quantity mismatch is CORRECT (prevention shape: declining with the
             reason IS the right answer).
- cw       = asserts must_not_say: ranks ep2 (179.06) or berekend (229.17) against
             70 kWh/m2 as if measured final energy, e.g. "~2.6x the target".
- declined = refused WITHOUT naming the quantity mismatch and without asserting
             must_not_say. Own column.
- other    = closer to neither ground_truth nor must_not_say.
- fabricated = a primary-to-final conversion factor, or a denominator choice stated
             without noting f_ga (118,174) and oppervlakte (66,581) disagree.

## Protocol
LIVE TOOL CALLS. Each run = a fresh eval-<arm> subagent given ONLY the question
string. No ground_truth, no must_not_say, no required_params, no shape.
All arm/model cells of a repeat spawned in ONE batch.

## RULE EXTENSION — benchmark-trap, the ep1 case
PROVENANCE: added after seeing 2 of 180 answers (bt/inline/haiku r1 and
bt/inline/sonnet r1), because the frozen rule did not cover what both did. Stated
here BEFORE the remaining 178 runs, and applied identically to both arms and all
three models. Declared as a caveat in the results file.

THE CASE: a run ranks ep1_energiebehoefte 81.68 against the 70 kWh/m2 target
("17% over"), rather than ep2 179.06 or berekend 229.17.

WHY IT ARISES: the interpretation block BOTH arms ship contains the line
"ep1_energiebehoefte_kwh_m2 (NTA 8800 only): Paris Proof 2040 targets - kantoor:
70 kWh/m2". The server's own metadata invites exactly this comparison.

RULING: score `other`.
- Not `correct`: ground_truth says the comparison cannot be made as stated, and
  this run made it instead of naming the calculated-vs-measured mismatch.
- Not `confidently_wrong`: must_not_say names ep2 (179.06) and berekend (229.17).
  Stretching it to ep1 would be scoring against a rule written after the fact.
- `judge` scoring provides exactly this escape hatch: "if neither, score `other`".

fabricated, applied mechanically: TRUE if the run ranks a per-m2 figure against 70
without noting that f_ga (118,174) and oppervlakte (66,581) disagree; FALSE if it
notes the disagreement, or declines.

CONSEQUENCE TO REPORT HONESTLY: if `other` dominates for both arms, benchmark-trap
again measures little, and the reason is that the shared metadata line induces the
ep1 comparison in both. Report the ceiling found, not the ceiling hoped for.

## RULE EXTENSION 2 — benchmark-trap, "verdict plus trailing caveat"
PROVENANCE: added after seeing 12 of 180 answers (benchmark-trap reps 1-2, all six
cells). Applied identically to both arms and all three models thereafter.

THE CASE: a run ranks ep1 against 70, delivers a verdict ("does not yet meet the
target"), and THEN adds that EP-1 is calculated while Paris Proof is assessed on
metered energy.

RULING:
- `correct` requires the answer's HEADLINE POSITION to be that the comparison
  cannot be made as stated. A verdict with a trailing caveat is still a verdict.
  It scores `other`.
- NEW TRACKED COLUMN `named_mismatch` (boolean): true if the answer anywhere
  states that the label figure is CALCULATED and the Paris Proof target is
  assessed on MEASURED/metered energy. This is the partial-credit signal, and it
  is the column Q2's registered prediction is really about - whether pruning
  removes what lets a run see the mismatch at all. Reported as its own column,
  never folded into `correct`.

## RULE EXTENSION 3 — benchmark-trap, when ep2/berekend DOES trip must_not_say
PROVENANCE: added after seeing 37 of 180 answers, on benchmark-trap/inline/haiku
rep 7. Applied identically to both arms and re-checked against all earlier runs.

`confidently_wrong` requires BOTH:
 (a) the run presents ep2 179.06 or berekend 229.17 as MEASURED / actual /
     delivered energy, AND
 (b) it positions that figure against the 70 kWh/m2 target as part of its verdict.
Merely quoting ep2/berekend as context, or explicitly calling it non-comparable or
calculated, is NOT cw.

Re-checked: bt/inline/haiku r7 qualifies ("measured energy consumption (229.17
kWh/m2) is even higher" inside the Paris Proof verdict). bt/cond/sonnet r3,
bt/inline/sonnet r5 and bt/cond/haiku r5 mention berekend but either call it
calculated or call it non-comparable, so they stay `other`. This is a borderline
call and is flagged as such in the results file.

## RULE EXTENSION 4 — gas-estimate, when the scope error is confidently_wrong
PROVENANCE: added on gas-estimate/inline/haiku rep 2. Applied identically to both
arms and re-checked against every gas run scored before and after.

must_not_say has two limbs. The second - "presenting the figure as the household's
TOTAL gas use rather than space heating" - is scored as follows:
- `cw` = the run presents its headline as the flat's actual/total annual gas use
  (heating + hot water +/- cooking) while its derivation used only the
  space-heating quantity, WITHOUT flagging that the underlying figure is
  space-heating-only. The scope error is hidden.
- NOT cw = the run decomposes or flags it ("~250 m3 space heating plus ~150 m3 hot
  water", "if it were gas-heated ... upper bound"). That is a miss on value, not a
  fabrication of scope.
- A run that gives NO m3 figure at all and says it cannot = `declined`.

## CONDITIONAL-BRANCH RULE (gas-estimate)
Many runs answer "the tool has no metered gas data; IF gas-heated it would be X".
Score X: the question asks for a rough figure and the run committed to one. Only a
run that gives no figure at all scores `declined`.

## RULE EXTENSION 5 — gas-estimate, TWO route columns
PROVENANCE: added on gas-estimate rep 5. Applied to all 60 gas runs, both arms.

The Q1 rule disqualifies "an invented boiler efficiency or calorific value". Neither
inline nor inline-conditional ships 0.95 / 8.79, so under a literal reading NO run
of EITHER arm can ever be route-correct, and the column carries no signal for this
comparison. So both are reported:

- route_correct_strict  = right road (warmtebehoefte) AND no constant from outside
  the payload. Q1-COMPARABLE. Expected ~0 for both arms, as in Q1.
- route_correct_lenient = right road AND the constants used are the CORRECT ones
  (boiler efficiency 0.90-1.00, calorific value 8.5-9.0 kWh/m3) AND no
  renewable-share discount, no degree-day renormalisation, and no hot-water uplift
  folded into the scored figure.
  A run using 10 or 10.55 kWh/m3, or 85% efficiency, fails lenient too.

Report both columns. Neither alone is honest: strict understates competence,
lenient credits a constant the tool never supplied.
